assessment: This is a well executed study that provides significant new insights and connections between protein structure, stability and function. Numerous sites of mutation are identified that activate the small GTPase Ras beyond the few cancer "hot spots" that predominate cancer genomics data. While cancer causing mutations selectively alter regulatory interactions with GTPase-activating proteins, careful biophysical analysis presented here leads to the conclusion that Ras is also activated by mutations that decrease stability (increase dynamics) short of unfolding. Thus, protein sensitivity to activating mutations can depend on the stability threshold in addition to regulatory interactions with binding partners.
